The program provides a strong foundation in data analytics, with courses on topics like machine learning, artificial intelligence, big data and data visualization. Students learn how to apply these techniques to real-world problems in their chosen field. The M.S. in Applied Data Science program at Clarkson University is available in-person or online, allowing students the flexibility to continue working or pursuing other opportunities while they study. The program can be completed on either a full- or part-time basis. This program is STEM designated.

Description: A Clarkson MBA develops graduates to become leaders and innovators in a fast-paced, technologically driven global marketplace. Students are challenged by a rigorous curriculum that emphasizes strategic thinking, ethical decision-making, and teamwork. In a Clarkson MBA classroom, students solve real-world problems for real companies, participate in national and international business competitions, and travel abroad on global business trips. The Clarkson MBA is offered on-campus at our Capital Region Campus in Schenectady, NY, and online. Students can choose to study on-campus or online, full-time or part-time. Our on-campus and online programs have the same curriculum and instructors. Our curriculum consists of nine core classes (27 credit hours) and three elective courses (9 credit hours). The core curriculum provides comprehensive coverage of key business functions. This includes the foundations of teamwork and leadership, as well as the analytical skills necessary for business problem-solving and innovation. It also instills the importance of social, ethical and environmental responsibility in today’s business world. Electives can be used to earn a concentration or to customize the program to best meet your needs.

Accredidation: Accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

Our AACSB-accredited Master of Business Administration in Healthcare Management program provides the crucial business management knowledge and healthcare industry expertise to effectively and efficiently lead a wide variety of healthcare-related organizations. You can select an online or on-campus MBA. The program culminates with a required capstone experience project for a healthcare organization. This hybrid program requires two weekend residencies per year at our Capital Region Campus in Schenectady, New York. You can also meet all requirements for the Lean Six Sigma Green Belt Certification.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

ProgramName: Master of Science in Healthcare Data Analytics
Requirements: All applicants should possess a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. To be considered for admission, a complete application will include the following: Online Application Form; Statement of Purpose; Resume or C.V.; Letters of Recommendation; Official Transcripts; Official test scores for the GRE or GMAT are not required but may be submitted to strengthen your application; For international applicants, an English proficiency test is required (see below for more information).
Description: The Master of Science in Healthcare Data Analytics program is a 36-credit-hour, fully online program for working professionals. The program’s curriculum provides a powerful combination of data analytics skills set in the context of the business of healthcare. Students will learn how to access, manage, analyze and transform data into actionable information that leads to improved patient care, enhanced efficiency and better outcomes. The program will equip students to use data to inform healthcare policy, management and clinical decision-making. Students will use the latest healthcare IT tools, programming languages and analytical software to understand and create data-driven insights. They will have access to a rich selection of industry datasets, case studies and projects.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

ProgramName: Master of Science in Clinical Leadership in Healthcare Management
Description: The Master of Science in Clinical Leadership in Healthcare Management is a 36-credit hour graduate degree that provides students with the business and leadership acumen for a management or leadership role in a clinical healthcare setting. The program is designed to transform the clinical expert into the clinical leader. The curriculum provides a foundation in leadership and the core functional business areas of healthcare management: finance, marketing, data analytics, human resources, quality, etc. The coursework is applied to the clinical setting, and the unique combination of leadership and management gives the clinical expert the skills and knowledge to effectively and efficiently lead the clinical team. The program is offered 100% online in 8-week terms, five times per year. You can begin at any one of five entry points. It can be completed on a part-time basis over two years or in one year on a full-time basis, depending on the number of courses taken per term.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

The certificate provides foundational knowledge in key areas of business, including accounting, finance, marketing and management. The certificate also serves as a gateway to the Clarkson MBA. All 15 credits from the Advanced Certificate in Business may be applied to the Clarkson MBA or MBA in Healthcare Management degree programs upon acceptance. The Advanced Certificate in Business is offered online and can be completed in as little as nine months. Students can start in either the fall or spring semesters.

Students also have the option of taking some or all courses in-person at our Capital Region Campus in Schenectady, New York. Description: Supply chain management (SCM) is the active management of the flow of goods and services. It includes all processes that transform raw materials into final products, from the point of origin to the point of consumption. Clarkson's nine-credit advanced certificate in SCM provides a solid foundation for those looking to advance or begin their career in this fast-growing field. Our curriculum covers the fundamentals of SCM, such as lean enterprise, operations management and logistics, as well as sustainability, technology management, and project management. The program addresses key SCM areas including: Development and management of a global supply chain. Use of analytics, technology and sustainable practices. Sourcing, procurement, and operations and logistics management.

Students learn advanced fundamentals and conduct independent research on a cutting-edge topic in chemical engineering. You'll complete the program with a written dissertation and an oral defense. Most students finish in about four years of full-time study after a Master of Science degree or about five years after a Bachelor of Science degree. We are committed to an inclusive and diverse environment. Learn more about our initiatives and campus groups. Our primary research thrusts in chemical engineering are: Advanced Materials Processing, Biomolecular Engineering, Complex Fluids and Nanotechnology, Process and Energy Systems Engineering.

However, applicants with other engineering and science degrees (e.g., chemistry, physics, materials science) are encouraged to apply and may be admitted with the provision that they complete a specified bridge program of undergraduate chemical engineering courses.

Our program allows you to deepen your expertise in the field. You will develop a sophisticated understanding of chemical engineering principles and practices. You will learn to apply these advanced concepts to solve complex problems in various industries. You can complete the 30-credit-hour program in one year. Customize your coursework to your career interests. Choose to complete a thesis and conduct research with our renowned faculty. Or opt for a non-thesis, project-based track. You can also further specialize your degree through one of three concentrations. Graduates of this program have gone on to work at companies like Pfizer, GlobalFoundries and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Civil & Environmental Engineering
Requirements: The following items are required to apply to the PhD in civil and environmental engineering program: An online application. A statement of purpose. A resume or C.V. Description: The Department of Civil & Environmental Engineering offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Science (MS), Master of Engineering (ME) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees. Our graduate students come from around the world and often go on to be leaders in industry and academia. As a student, you will have opportunities to work closely with our world-renowned faculty on cutting-edge research in a wide array of topics. In particular, we specialize in environmental and water resources engineering, geotechnical and materials engineering, and structural and construction engineering. The doctor of philosophy degree requires a minimum of 90 credit hours beyond the bachelor's degree. A minimum of 39 of these hours must be in coursework. In addition, there are seminar, residency and teaching requirements. You will work with a faculty advisor and advisory committee to plan your coursework and research, and your studies will culminate in a dissertation with a final oral defense.

You may also qualify for our tuition-scholarship program.

It is designed to prepare students for a wide range of professional careers in the architecture-engineering-construction (AEC) industry. The core curriculum provides students with knowledge of the business and management aspects of the construction industry. As a Construction Engineering Management student, you’ll learn the technical aspects of construction materials, equipment, planning, scheduling and cost estimating. You’ll also develop the managerial skills necessary for a successful career in the construction industry. The coursework integrates construction engineering with business management. You’ll become equipped with the ability to manage complex construction projects.

Graduate students matriculated in other programs at Clarkson may also apply for the certificate.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Electrical and Computer Engineering
Department: Wallace H. Coulter School of Engineering
Description:
The Doctor of Philosophy in electrical and computer engineering program at Clarkson University emphasizes a close working relationship between students and faculty. As a result, our graduate students are highly sought after for positions in industry, research and academia.

The graduate program provides a strong foundation in the fundamentals while encouraging students to pursue cutting-edge research. You can conduct research in one of four primary areas. This includes areas with a large number of faculty, including power and energy systems and communications and signal processing. Read more about research below.

You can also work with faculty outside the department, such as through one of our world-renowned research centers. This includes the Center for Air and Aquatic Resources Engineering and Sciences (CAARES), the Center for Advanced Materials Processing (CAMP) and the Institute for a Sustainable Environment (ISE).

All full-time students in the PhD program are supported with a stipend and tuition waiver, most often through a teaching or research assistantship.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering
Department: Wallace H. Coulter School of Engineering
Description: The Master of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering is a research-based master’s degree program designed to deepen your fundamental knowledge of electrical and computer engineering and support your independent research experience. Our program prepares you for a research-and-development-oriented career or for more advanced studies at the doctoral level. In particular, this degree is intended for students who have a strong aptitude for research and are looking to push beyond the limits of current technologies. You will develop an in-depth understanding of advanced topics in electrical and computer engineering. You will acquire the skills necessary to perform independent research. You will learn how to organize and present your results professionally in both written and oral forms. You will be better prepared to make a long-term impact on society in your field of choice. The program requires 30 credit hours, including six to 12 credit hours of thesis research. The program typically takes four semesters to complete. Students are assigned an advisor in their general area of interest for the first semester. By the end of the first semester, students select their research advisor and thesis topic.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

Our graduate power program includes a broad set of courses, including power systems analysis, protection, dynamics and control; power electronics; renewable energy systems and electric machines.

Description: The electric power system is arguably the largest and most complex machine ever built. The engineering challenges are vast, with opportunities ranging from designing the next generation of smart grid technology to developing systems for integrating renewable energy sources. To meet these demands, the Advanced Certificate in Power Systems Engineering program at Clarkson will prepare you for a rewarding career in the power industry. You'll gain a fundamental understanding of power systems and be prepared to perform advanced engineering tasks in your specialty. Through a combination of on-campus and online coursework, this nine-credit-hour program can be completed in as little as nine months, and the curriculum overlaps significantly with our Master of Science in Electrical Engineering program. This allows you to apply what you've learned toward a master's degree, should you choose to continue your education.

Description: Materials are all around us, from the concrete in our sidewalks to the glass on our phones. Research at Clarkson in materials science and engineering focuses on advancing the performance of existing materials and developing new ones to help solve some of the world's most pressing issues. Our PhD in Materials Science & Engineering is an interdisciplinary program administered by the Departments of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, Chemistry and Biomolecular Science, Civil and Environmental Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, and Mechanical and Aeronautical Engineering. As a student in our program, you will have access to our world-class research facilities and the opportunity to work alongside faculty who are experts in their fields. You will also have the opportunity to participate in our research centers, including the Center for Advanced Materials Processing (CAMP), a New York State Center for Advanced Technology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

ProgramName: Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
Description: The Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering is a multidisciplinary program aimed at providing a graduate-level education in materials engineering for students with undergraduate degrees in engineering or the physical sciences. The program provides an education in the fundamental science and engineering of materials. It also allows students to specialize in a materials sub-discipline to prepare them for a job in the industry or to continue their education toward a PhD.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical Engineering
Department: Wallace H. Coulter School of Engineering

Description:
The Mechanical Engineering PhD program provides you with the skills and training needed to be a leader in the mechanical engineering industry or in in academia. You will receive an advanced education in the fundamentals of mechanical engineering while also specializing in an area of your choice.
A PhD in mechanical engineering will enable you to make high-level contributions to the field. You can conduct high-level research at a university or a national lab. Or you can pursue a career in industry, including roles in R&D, manufacturing and consulting. Many of our students are also interested in becoming educators.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

Department: Wallace H. Coulter School of Engineering
Concentration: ['Solid Mechanics, Materials and Manufacturing', 'Fluid Mechanics, Thermal and Energy Sciences', 'Robotics, Controls and Dynamical Systems']
Description: Our Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering is a flexible program that allows you to tailor your curriculum to your specific interests and goals. Core areas of study include solid mechanics, fluid mechanics and robotics. You can choose to write a master's thesis or opt for a non-thesis, project-based track. You can earn the degree in just one year of full-time study. You can also pursue a master's degree part-time. Most classes are held in the late afternoon or evening for the convenience of working professionals.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

Description: Clarkson's one-year Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) program is designed for individuals who have a bachelor's degree in a specific subject area and want to become a teacher in that subject. The MAT program is field-based and requires two semesters of clinical practice in our partner schools. Our graduates are highly sought-after by school districts throughout New York and other states. We have a nearly 100 percent placement rate, and our alumni have been recognized with state and national teaching awards.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Occupational Therapy
Requirements: A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university. A minimum overall GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Successful completion of all prerequisite coursework with a C or better. Submission of the Occupational Therapist Centralized Application Service (OTCAS) application. A minimum of 20 hours of observation/volunteer experience in one or more occupational therapy settings is required. Three letters of reference. Personal essay. Successful completion of an interview with a member of the Clarkson University OT faculty.
Description: The Master of Science in Occupational Therapy program at Clarkson University provides a strong foundation in the sciences, professional skills, and research and prepares students to become highly skilled, ethical, and compassionate occupational therapists. Students will be prepared to enter a variety of practice settings with a comprehensive understanding of the profession's history, theory, and evidence-based practice. Our curriculum emphasizes hands-on learning, clinical reasoning, and interprofessional collaboration, ensuring that our graduates are well-equipped to meet the diverse needs of their clients and communities. This program culminates in a capstone experience, allowing students to integrate their knowledge and skills in a focused area of practice.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs
Accredidation: The entry-level occupational therapy master’s degree program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) of the American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA), located at 6116 Executive Boulevard, Suite 200, North Bethesda, MD 20852-4929. ACOTE’s telephone number c/o AOTA is (301) 652-AOTA and its Web address is www.acoteonline.org. Graduates of the program will be eligible to sit for the national certification examination for the occupational therapist administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT). After successful completion of this exam, the individual will be an Occupational Therapist, Registered (OTR). In addition, most states require licensure in order to practice; however, state licenses are usually based on the results of the NBCOT Certification Examination. Note that a felony conviction may affect a graduate’s ability to sit for the NBCOT certification examination or attain state licensure.

ProgramName: Doctor of Physical Therapy
Description: The Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) program at Clarkson University is a three-year graduate program that prepares students for a career as a physical therapist. Our program combines a strong foundation in the basic and clinical sciences with extensive hands-on experience in our state-of-the-art laboratories and diverse clinical settings. Students in our DPT program learn from expert faculty who are dedicated teachers, clinicians and researchers. Clarkson's DPT program prides itself on a low student-to-faculty ratio, which allows for personalized attention and mentorship. Our curriculum emphasizes evidence-based practice, critical thinking and professional development, ensuring our graduates are well-prepared to meet the challenges of the evolving healthcare landscape. Graduates of our program are highly sought after by employers and have a strong record of success on the national licensure examination. The Doctor of Physical Therapy program begins in the summer and is based at Clarkson's Capital Region Campus in Schenectady, New York.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs
Accredidation: The Doctor of Physical Therapy Program at Clarkson University is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE), 3030 Potomac Ave., Ste 100, Alexandria, VA 22305-3085; phone: 703-706-3245; email: accreditation@apta.org; website: http://www.capteonline.org. If needing to contact the program/institution directly, please call 518-631-9870 or email dpt@clarkson.edu.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Physician Assistant Studies
Description:
The Clarkson University Master of Science in Physician Assistant Studies program has a 28-month curriculum that prepares you for a rewarding career as a physician assistant (PA). PAs are licensed medical providers who work in all medical and surgical specialties on healthcare teams with physicians and other providers. Our mission is to educate and develop compassionate, skilled and knowledgeable physician assistants who will provide high-quality healthcare to the people of the North Country and other communities.

The program philosophy is one of commitment to our students and to the communities we serve. Our faculty and staff are dedicated to supporting our students as they learn and grow through our program. Our primary goal is to educate PAs to provide superior medical care and to become leaders in their communities. We expect a high level of professionalism from our students. We are committed to teaching and modeling the importance of teamwork, integrity, intellectual curiosity and caring. We offer our students a variety of educational opportunities in diverse communities in upstate New York. We believe that an awareness of the many challenges of providing medical care in a rural setting is a key component to a comprehensive medical education. We support the communities we serve by teaching our students to be mindful of and to address the social determinants of health that impact the wellness of individuals and communities.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs
Accredidation: The Accreditation Review Commission on Education for the Physician Assistant, Inc. (ARC-PA) has granted Accreditation-Continued status to the Clarkson University Physician Assistant Program sponsored by Clarkson University. Accreditation-Continued is an accreditation status granted when a currently accredited program is in compliance with the ARC-PA Standards.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Bioethics
Requirements: Online application form, Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, Statement of purpose, Two letters of recommendation, Resume or curriculum vitae
Description: The Master of Science in Bioethics is a 31-credit-hour program that introduces students to the major areas of bioethics. Students develop the necessary background and skills to analyze and resolve complex moral problems and dilemmas in medicine, research and health policy. This program provides an excellent foundation for a number of professions including medicine, law, nursing and other allied health professions as well as for those seeking doctoral level work in bioethics or a related field. Students can complete all degree requirements completely online. Students may also begin study in either the fall or spring semester. All graduates of the program complete a major research paper that may be submitted for publication to an academic journal. Students typically complete the program in two years, although it can be completed in as little as 12 months. Each student is also provided with a faculty mentor who assists him or her with all aspects of the program, from course selection to the completion of the major research paper. The Master of Science degree in bioethics is granted jointly by Clarkson University and the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai in New York City.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs
ScholarshipPercentage: A 30 percent tuition scholarship is automatically awarded to all accepted students. Clarkson alumni and professionals in partner programs receive a 50 percent tuition scholarship.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Bioscience and Biotechnology
Description: The Ph.D. in bioscience and biotechnology is an interdisciplinary program that combines strengths in biology and chemistry with engineering to offer a unique doctoral program. The program is a part of the core research focus at Clarkson's Center for Advanced Materials Processing (CAMP) and the Center for Air Resources Engineering and Science (CARES). Doctoral students may also be affiliated with Clarkson's Beacon Institute for Rivers and Estuaries. The program is jointly administered by the Departments of Biology and Chemistry & Biomolecular Science. Research opportunities are provided by Clarkson faculty who are well-recognized and funded in their individual fields. Research focus areas include but are not limited to: Biomaterials, Bioinformatics & Biocomputational Modeling, Environmental Science & Biotechnology, and Molecular & Cell Biology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

ProgramName: Master of Science in Bioscience and Biotechnology
Requirements: For admission to the MS in Bioscience and Biotechnology program, applicants must have a bachelor’s degree in biology, chemistry, or a related field. Undergraduate coursework should include general biology and chemistry, organic chemistry, and calculus. Prospective students can apply online. The required application materials are a completed online application form, a statement of purpose, a current resume, official college transcripts, and three letters of recommendation.
Description:
The M.S. in Bioscience & Biotechnology is offered through the Department of Biology in Clarkson's School of Arts & Sciences. The program has a strong research emphasis. It is intended for students with bachelor's degrees who wish to further their training for careers in the rapidly growing fields of bioscience and biotechnology.

Our state-of-the-art facilities offer a rich environment for research. This includes our facilities in the Center for Applied Science & Engineering (CASE), which opened in 2021. The program also draws from our strong connections with biotech companies, including those in the Trudeau Institute business incubator. Our proximity to the Adirondack Mountains provides unique opportunities to study environmental biology and biotechnology.

Our bioscience and biotechnology graduate program is small. This allows for personalized interaction between students and faculty. We offer a thesis-based degree with opportunities for cutting-edge research in a wide range of modern biological disciplines. These include molecular and cell biology, genomics, immunology and biotechnology. Faculty in the Department of Biology are actively engaged in research that crosses disciplines. They also work with faculty in chemistry, engineering and physics. Students are engaged in projects ranging from the development of novel anti-cancer drugs to the study of social behavior. They also explore the genetic basis of diseases and use DNA-based methods to understand ecosystem functioning.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships, Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemistry
Requirements: Applicants must have a BS or MS degree in chemistry or a closely related field. They also must satisfy the general admission requirements of the Clarkson Graduate School.
Concentration: Analytical/Inorganic/Physical Chemistry, Biomolecular Chemistry, Materials/Polymer Chemistry, Organic/Medicinal Chemistry
Description: The Department of Chemistry and Biomolecular Science offers a program of study leading to the Doctor of Philosophy degree in chemistry. The PhD degree is a research-based degree that requires a dissertation based on original research. It typically takes four to five years to complete the degree requirements. The research specialties of our faculty span the traditional areas of analytical, inorganic, physical, and organic chemistry and biochemistry. Much of our research is interdisciplinary, with active collaborations with faculty from other departments, including biology, physics, chemical engineering, and mechanical engineering. Clarkson's Center for Advanced Materials Processing (CAMP) is another area of active interdisciplinary research and the intellectual center for a number of high-tech industries.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: For admission to the Graduate School, you need to hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. Clarkson requires a minimum 3.0 undergraduate GPA (on a 4.0 scale) for admission to our graduate programs. If your GPA is below 3.0, you may still be considered for provisional admission. A complete application consists of a completed online application, a statement of purpose, a resume or curriculum vitae (CV), official transcripts from all institutions attended, and three letters of recommendation.
Concentration: Analytical Chemistry, Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Physical Chemistry, Materials Chemistry
Description: The Master of Science in Chemistry is a two-year research-based degree in which students work closely with their research advisors on a research project that will ultimately be submitted for their thesis. Students are prepared to go into a doctoral program or an industrial position. The department has five major research areas: Analytical Chemistry, Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Physical Chemistry, and Materials Chemistry. Students will take courses in these areas and participate in a vibrant seminar program. Students must pass a series of cumulative exams in their chosen area of study, write a publishable thesis, and defend it to complete the degree.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mathematics
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) program in mathematics is offered through the Department of Mathematics. The Department of Mathematics at Clarkson has a long history of national recognition in applied mathematics. The program provides a broad background in several areas of applied mathematics and expertise in an area of specialization. Students become experienced researchers by completing a dissertation under the direction of a faculty advisor. The PhD in mathematics gives students training and experience that allows them to pursue careers in academia, industry or government.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition coverage and a stipend of about $28,000 a year

ProgramName: Master of Science in Mathematics
Description:
Our Master of Science in Mathematics program is designed for you if you love math and want to apply it to solve problems in a range of fields. We will prepare you for a professional career in industry or government, or for further graduate study.

Our faculty are active researchers and dedicated teachers in a wide range of areas in both pure and applied mathematics. They are accessible to students and integrate them into research projects. As an MS student, you will have the opportunity to participate in and present your research at seminars and conferences.

We provide a supportive, collaborative environment where you can explore your individual interests. You will complete a thesis or research project in your area of interest under the direction of a faculty advisor.

Our recent graduates have found employment at companies such as the Naval Nuclear Laboratory, The Hartford Insurance, the U.S. Census Bureau and Trans-American Financial. Others have gone on to PhD programs at schools like the University of North Carolina and Baylor University.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.clarkson.edu/academics/graduate/programs

Description: The Department of Physics offers a flexible program of study leading to the PhD degree. Students can design a program that best suits their academic and research goals. The physics program offers a diverse curriculum with specialization in many areas of physics. The program also emphasizes collaborative interdisciplinary research. A physics degree prepares students to enter numerous STEM careers in academia, industry and government labs. Clarkson faculty are nationally and internationally recognized for their research. Research is sponsored by federal agencies, including the National Science Foundation, the Department of Energy, the Department of Defense and NASA.

Description: As society and industry increasingly face complex issues related to energy production and use, the demand for T-shaped professionals who can bridge the gap between engineering and management in the energy industry has never been greater. The Advanced Certificate in Business of Energy from Clarkson University will give you the knowledge you need to enter the dynamic field of energy.

Requirements: Online Application Form, Résumé, Statement of purpose, Two letters of recommendation, Official transcripts. International applicants whose native language is not English must submit a TOEFL or IELTS score.
Description: The advanced certificate in environmental management provides professionals with the skills needed to make informed decisions that balance environmental concerns and economic realities. The program is ideal for those in the environmental sector who require formal training in management, as well as those in business and other fields who need to expand their knowledge of environmental issues. The coursework offers training in the core areas of environmental regulation, environmental and natural resource economics, environmental systems analysis and project management. The certificate consists of four required courses, all of which are offered online.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Department: Wallace H. Coulter School of Engineering
Description: At Clarkson, our program has an excellent reputation for preparing students for successful careers in the aerospace engineering profession, from designing satellites to developing the next generation of aircraft. As an aerospace engineering student, you will learn the fundamentals of aerodynamics, astrodynamics, aerospace materials and structures, and propulsion. You will also learn about stability and control of aerospace vehicles. You will learn to use computer-aided tools and gain hands-on experience in our state-of-the-art labs and facilities. We emphasize teamwork and interdisciplinary projects, which is why our graduates are highly sought after by employers. The first year is part of the Clarkson Common Experience, which all students take. During your sophomore year, you'll take introductory courses in mechanical and aeronautical engineering, as well as foundational courses in engineering, mathematics and physics. Then, you'll specialize in aeronautical engineering during your junior and senior years. You'll complete a yearlong capstone design project during your senior year, working as a team to tackle a real-world problem from a corporate sponsor or a faculty-led research project.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in American Politics
Concentration: data analytics
Description: Clarkson's political science major stands out for its strong focus on American politics and public policy and its unique integration of data analytics and social science methods. Students receive rigorous training in both qualitative and quantitative research methods to examine the processes, outcomes and theories of political systems. As a political science major at Clarkson, you will work closely with faculty who are active researchers, publishing cutting-edge studies of public opinion, elections and political behavior, constitutional law, environmental policy, and U.S. foreign policy.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics and Statistics
Requirements: To apply for admission to Clarkson as a first-year student, you will need to submit the following: A completed application using the Clarkson Application or the Common Application; An official high school transcript; At least one letter of recommendation; A personal essay.
Description: Applied mathematics is the language of science and engineering. Mathematical and statistical modeling are essential tools for solving problems in a huge range of fields, from physics and chemistry to business and finance. At Clarkson, you will learn to use those tools to solve complex real-world problems. Our project-based curriculum challenges you to find creative solutions and communicate them effectively. You'll master a variety of mathematical techniques. But more importantly, you will learn how to approach problems from a quantitative perspective. You will also become proficient in using industry-standard software and gain valuable hands-on experience through research projects, cooperative education (co-op) opportunities and internships. As a student in the applied mathematics and statistics program, you will have opportunities to work with faculty on research. Our main research areas are in dynamical systems, mathematical biology, statistics and optimization.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Architectural and Facilities Engineering
Department: Wallace H. Coulter School of Engineering
Concentration: Construction Engineering Management
Description:
Architectural and facilities engineers oversee the entire life cycle of a building. They play a role in the design, construction and maintenance of buildings, making sure they are safe and comfortable for occupants, as well as efficient and sustainable. As an architectural and facilities engineering major, you'll gain the technical knowledge to design building systems. This includes:

- Electrical and lighting systems
- Heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC)
- Plumbing
- Structural systems

You'll also get a broad education in the other aspects of building life cycles, such as construction engineering and project management. Our curriculum gives you a broad education in architectural and facilities engineering, as well as the opportunity to specialize. All students take common courses in their first two years. You'll take more specialized courses in your junior and senior years. You can also further customize your degree through our Construction Engineering Management concentration. Or, you can pursue focus areas like sustainable design, construction engineering management and smart building technology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Arts, Culture and Technology

If you choose to submit scores, we will accept either the SAT or ACT. We will superscore both tests; Essay - Your application essay helps us get to know you better. Please submit one with your application.
Concentration: ['Creative Technology & Experience Design', 'Music, Media & Production', 'Visual Arts & Design']
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Arts, Culture and Technology (ACT) is an interdisciplinary program that teaches you how to bridge the connections between technology and creative applications in the humanities, arts and social sciences. As a student in the ACT program, you will develop marketable skills in one of three concentrations while building a portfolio of work and learning from faculty who are creative professionals in their fields. You'll gain a core understanding of design principles and develop an entrepreneurial mindset to successfully launch your career or your own enterprise in creative technology. Students in the program must declare one of three concentrations: Creative Technology & Experience Design; Music, Media & Production; and Visual Arts & Design. They can also earn an accelerated bachelor's/master's degree with a Master of Science in Human-Centered Design & Innovation.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology
Requirements: To apply for admission, you'll need to submit an application (either the Common Application or the Clarkson Application), your official high school transcript, and one letter of recommendation. International students may have additional requirements, like proof of English proficiency.
Concentration: ['pre-dental', 'pre-medical', 'pre-physician assistant', 'pre-veterinary', 'pre-physical therapy advising track']
Description: As a biology major at Clarkson, you will gain a strong foundation in modern biological principles and related sciences. You'll learn about biological processes at the molecular, cellular, organismal and ecological levels. You will also develop proficiency in modern laboratory techniques and a deep appreciation for the scientific method. Our program is tailored to your interests and career goals. Choose from four pre-professional tracks: pre-dental, pre-medical, pre-physician assistant and pre-veterinary. These tracks provide you with all of the necessary prerequisites to apply to professional schools in these fields after you graduate. We also offer a biomedical science & technology minor, as well as a pre-physical therapy advising track. No matter what path you choose, you'll be able to work closely with our faculty, who are conducting cutting-edge research in a wide variety of biological fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomolecular Science
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Biomolecular Science (BMS) is an interdisciplinary program jointly administered by the Departments of Biology and Chemistry & Biomolecular Science. The program offers a unique blend of biology, chemistry, mathematics and physics that focuses on the molecular basis of biological processes. The BMS major prepares students for graduate school in the biomolecular sciences, as well as for medical, dental or veterinary school. Students will also be well-qualified for jobs in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industries.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration
Concentration: ['Business Intelligence & Data Analytics', 'Economics', 'Entrepreneurship', 'Financial Information & Analysis', 'Global Supply Chain Management', 'Human Resource Management', 'Information Systems & Business Processes', 'Marketing', 'Mathematical Economics']
Description:
Do you want to develop the knowledge and skills needed to lead, manage and thrive in today's global business world? The business administration major in the Reh School of Business can prepare you.

As a business administration major, you'll take core classes in accounting, finance, law, management and marketing. You will then select two concentrations and a professional elective from among the following areas:

- Business Intelligence & Data Analytics
- Economics
- Entrepreneurship
- Financial Information & Analysis
- Global Supply Chain Management
- Human Resource Management
- Information Systems & Business Processes
- Marketing
- Mathematical Economics

You can also select from concentrations offered within other Clarkson schools. For example, if you want to run an engineering firm, you could combine your business administration major with a concentration in electrical engineering. You could also pursue an engineering and management major or a minor in business.

This major prepares you to work in a variety of industries, such as business, government and not-for-profit organizations. It offers a broad background in business, allowing you to tailor your curriculum to your unique interests and career goals.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.
Accredidation: All of our undergraduate and graduate business programs are accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Analytics
Department: David D. Reh School of Business
Description: Business analytics is the practice of using data to drive business decisions. Business analysts develop new insights and an understanding of business performance based on data and statistical methods. It requires the ability to collect, process, analyze and interpret data. This includes an understanding of data sources, file structures and data management techniques. Using business analytics, organizations are able to make better decisions and gain a competitive advantage. At Clarkson, you will major in business analytics and learn how to collect, process, analyze and interpret data. In a world with seemingly endless information, employers need people with these skills to inform business strategies. The business analytics major at Clarkson is structured to give you broad exposure to fundamental business analytics principles and practices. You can also customize your focus through various electives in accounting, economics, finance, information systems, marketing and supply chain management. The undergraduate business analytics degree is also designated as a STEM (science, technology, engineering and math) program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Intelligence and Data Analytics
Requirements: To apply, first-year students must submit a completed Common Application or Clarkson Application, an official high school transcript, one letter of recommendation from a school counselor or teacher, and a personal essay. Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for most applicants.
Department: David D. Reh School of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Business Intelligence and Data Analytics (BIDA) is a STEM-designated business degree. The BIDA program teaches you how to manage and leverage data to generate business insights. You will take courses in data mining, business analytics, management information systems, supply chain modeling, business forecasting, financial modeling, marketing research and statistics. You'll also learn the foundations of business, with courses in accounting, finance, marketing, management, operations and more. Data is big business, and it is a driving force behind almost every business decision being made today. Graduates with business intelligence and data analytics skills are in high demand in the workforce. The World Economic Forum, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, McKinsey Global Institute and others predict that jobs in this field will grow much faster than average through 2030.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Department: Wallace H. Coulter School of Engineering
Concentration: ['Biomolecular Engineering', 'Advanced Materials', 'Process Engineering', 'Business']
Description: Chemical engineers take what chemists do in a lab, apply fundamental engineering, chemistry and biology principles, and use it to make products and processes that are available on a larger, industrial scale. The Bachelor of Science degree in chemical engineering at Clarkson provides a core chemical engineering education that is second to none in the nation. It also has the flexibility to enable you to pursue your interests in a broad range of related areas. In addition to core chemical engineering coursework, you can pursue minors and concentrations in a variety of fields, from business to biomolecular engineering to environmental engineering. You can further customize your studies by pursuing undergraduate research opportunities. Chemical engineering graduates must be able to think critically and analytically when solving problems. You'll take a lot of challenging courses during your time in this program, and you'll work in laboratories and on a variety of project-based assignments. You will learn to work in teams, often with students in other engineering disciplines, to design systems, processes and equipment for chemical engineering-based industries. You will become familiar with the equipment and techniques used in chemical engineering practice. You'll gain an understanding of the professional and ethical responsibilities of chemical engineers and their impact on safety and society.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.
Accredidation: Our chemical engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry
Concentration: Biomolecular Chemistry, Chemical Science
Description: Chemistry is the central science that studies matter and its properties at the atomic and molecular level. As a chemistry major, you will study the composition, structure, properties and change of matter in all its forms, from the simplest atoms and molecules to complex biological systems. Our curriculum provides you with a strong foundation in the core areas of chemistry: analytical, biochemistry, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry. You will also have the opportunity to participate in research with our faculty, who are experts in their fields. In addition to classroom learning, you will gain hands-on experience in our modern and well-equipped laboratories. You will learn to use state-of-the-art instrumentation and techniques, and you will develop the skills to design and conduct experiments, analyze data and communicate your results. You will also have the opportunity to present your research at regional and national conferences, and to publish your work in peer-reviewed journals.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Cognitive Neuroscience

Description: Why study cognitive neuroscience at Clarkson? How do we learn? How do we remember? How does our brain function? These are just some of the questions we ask in the cognitive neuroscience program. As a cognitive neuroscience major at Clarkson, you will investigate how our brains work. You will learn about the relationship between the brain and human behavior. You will study how we pay attention, learn, solve problems, make decisions and use language. You will also study normal and abnormal brain functioning in relation to psychological disorders and diseases. You will have opportunities to complete research projects with faculty who are experts in fields such as neuropsychology and cognitive development. You will also learn valuable research skills, including hypothesis generation, experimental design and data analysis. These skills will prepare you for a variety of cognitive neuroscience careers and other professions.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering

Description: Computer engineering is a synergy of electrical engineering and computer science. Our students learn to design, implement, and test computer hardware and software for embedded systems and general-purpose computers. At Clarkson, we offer a rich lab environment where our students can apply what they learn in the classroom. You'll take part in research, co-ops and other hands-on learning experiences. In the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department, our expert faculty conduct research in areas like artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, data and systems, robotics, power systems, communications and networking, and cybersecurity. As a computer engineering major at Clarkson, you can customize your education to align with your career goals. This makes you more marketable, with many of our students receiving job offers well before they graduate. With our extensive list of technical and free electives, you can design a computer engineering program that's perfect for you. Our faculty can guide you in choosing electives based on your interests. Description:
The Bachelor of Science degree in engineering studies is an interdisciplinary engineering program designed for students who have a strong interest in engineering, but who may not wish to become licensed professional engineers. The program provides the flexibility to combine a solid engineering core with a concentration of courses in another professional field. Examples include pre-law, pre-med, engineering management, business, technical communications and liberal arts. This degree is not accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET.

The Bachelor of Science in Engineering Studies is designed to be very flexible in the final year and a half of study. Students complete a strong, broad-based engineering core that provides a solid technical background. In the junior and senior years, students work with an academic advisor to develop an individual plan of study that includes a suite of technical specialty courses and a sequence of courses in a non-engineering professional field. Engineering Studies is an ideal degree for those students who wish to pursue careers at the interface of engineering and other disciplines, for example, in technical sales, law, management or medicine.

Description: Environmental engineers use the principles of engineering, soil science, biology and chemistry to develop solutions to environmental problems. They are involved in efforts to improve recycling, waste disposal, public health, and water and air pollution control. They also address global issues, such as unsafe drinking water, climate change, and environmental sustainability. Environmental engineers design, plan, and implement measures to prevent, control, or remediate environmental hazards. They may work on waste treatment, wastewater treatment, site remediation, or pollution control technology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Health Science
Department: Coulter School of Engineering and School of Arts & Sciences
Description: Environmental health science focuses on the link between the environment and human health. Environmental health science professionals serve on the front lines, protecting us from threats in our environment. They work to ensure the air we breathe, the water we drink, the food we eat and the communities we live in are safe. This is a STEM-based degree at the intersection of environmental science, chemistry, biology and public health. Our degree provides you with a strong scientific background to assess environmental problems and their effects on human health. Through our challenging curriculum and unique hands-on opportunities, we'll teach you the skills needed to create solutions to these complex problems. Our program is nationally accredited by the National Environmental Health Science and Protection Accreditation Council (EHAC), making us one of only 30 accredited undergraduate environmental health programs in the nation. This accreditation allows our graduates to enter the U.S. Public Health Service as commissioned officers. As part of the Institute for a Sustainable Environment, our students learn from and conduct research with expert faculty in a wide variety of areas. Our small class sizes allow our faculty to work one-on-one with students to meet their academic and career goals. We also work closely with our extensive alumni network to develop professional opportunities for our students. Through our interdisciplinary curriculum, you'll learn: The scientific principles behind major environmental problems, such as air pollution, water pollution and climate change. How environmental contaminants affect human health and the science of toxicology. The essential elements of epidemiology and how to investigate disease outbreaks. The principles of industrial hygiene and how to protect worker health and safety. How to apply risk assessment principles to evaluate and manage environmental health risks. The laws and policies that protect both environmental and public health. The hands-on skills to assess environmental quality and exposure in our state-of-the-art laboratories.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.
Accredidation: Our program is nationally accredited by the National Environmental Health Science and Protection Accreditation Council (EHAC).

As a mechanical engineer, you will influence the design of all types of products and systems, including cars, planes, power plants, robots, biomedical devices and more. You will find that our curriculum combines classroom instruction with hands-on lab and design experience, which gives you valuable professional skills. ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Philosophy
Description: Philosophy is the study of the fundamental questions of human existence. What is knowledge? What is the nature of reality? What does it mean to be a good person, and what is the best way to live? Philosophers explore these questions with creativity and rigorous logical analysis. They develop strong skills in critical thinking, reading and writing. They learn how to analyze and construct arguments. And they learn how to express themselves with clarity and precision. Our program offers courses in traditional branches of philosophy, like logic, ethics, metaphysics and the history of philosophy, as well as in fields of applied ethics, like bioethics and environmental ethics. Philosophy can be studied on its own or as a second major. It is especially popular as a double major with engineering, science, business and pre-health programs. This is because the analytical and communication skills provided by a philosophy education are vital to success in any profession. Philosophy majors have some of the highest acceptance rates to law school and medical school, and they have the highest mid-career salary of any humanities major.

At Clarkson, a Bachelor of Science in Physics goes beyond the theoretical. Our world-class faculty will guide you as you apply what you learn in the classroom to real-world challenges in our state-of-the-art labs and research facilities. You can work with faculty on cutting-edge research in a wide range of areas, including condensed matter physics, optics, statistical mechanics, complex systems and nonlinear dynamics. In addition to a core curriculum of physics courses, the program offers technical electives that will help you gain skills for life after graduation. In your junior and senior years, you can conduct a research project as part of your senior capstone experience.

Description: Political science is the systematic study of power: who has it, why they have it and how they use it. The major is designed for students who are intellectually curious about the major political questions of our time. It provides a deeper understanding of political events, ideas and institutions. You will gain in-depth knowledge of how political and governmental systems operate. You will examine the impact that public policies have on society, the economy and everyday life. Our curriculum will prepare you to make a difference in society. You'll be taught by faculty who are active researchers, who publish in leading academic journals and who are committed to teaching excellence. Small class sizes promote close student-faculty interaction and mentoring. In addition to a set of core courses, you will choose from a rich array of courses in five areas: American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory and public policy. The political science major will give you in-depth knowledge, analytical skills and practical experience. You will understand how political actors behave and make choices. You will learn to form compelling arguments. And you will gain advanced writing and communication skills. You can further hone these skills in our honors program, which culminates in a thesis you will present to department faculty.

Description: The pre-medical sciences major is an interdisciplinary program designed for students who want a strong science foundation for careers in medicine and other health professions. This program provides the foundational coursework required for admission to a number of professional graduate programs in the health sciences. Through a rigorous and flexible science curriculum, students are prepared to excel on standardized admissions tests and in their professional school programs. A distinguishing feature of Clarkson's health sciences programs is that students work with a dedicated pre-health advisor starting their first year to select coursework and plan professional development activities that match their career aspirations. This combination of a rigorous curriculum and comprehensive advisement has allowed our students to be highly successful in gaining admission to their professional school of choice. The curriculum can be tailored to meet the entrance requirements for a variety of health professional programs, including: Pre-Dental, Pre-Medical, Pre-Occupational Therapy, Pre-Optometry, Pre-Pharmacy, Pre-Physical Therapy, Pre-Physician Assistant, Pre-Podiatry, Pre-Veterinary. This major cannot be combined with the following majors: biology, biomolecular science, chemistry, or physics. It can be paired with a humanities, social sciences or business major as part of a double major. In such cases, this program would serve as the science component of the student's education.

Our curriculum is specifically designed to meet or exceed the requirements of most DPT programs. You can major in any field you wish, so long as you meet the prerequisites for physical therapy school. Many of our pre-physical therapy students major in biology, psychology or biomolecular science. Our health professions advisors work closely with you to ensure you are meeting all requirements for DPT school. Our students are well-prepared for entry into physical therapy programs. Over the last 10 years, 87 percent of our graduates have been accepted into physical therapy schools. Clarkson also has several articulation agreements with graduate programs that give our students an advantage in the admission process. The most popular of these is our direct-entry pathway for our undergraduate students into our own Doctor of Physical Therapy program. Our students can apply as early as their junior year for guaranteed admission, so long as they meet the specific requirements.

Physician assistants (PAs) are in high demand. These highly skilled healthcare professionals work in all medical and surgical specialties. They work in a variety of settings, including hospitals, clinics, physician offices, nursing homes and other healthcare facilities. They perform physical exams, order and interpret diagnostic tests, diagnose and treat illnesses, assist in surgery, and write prescriptions. Clarkson's Pre-Physician Assistant Program is not a major, but a concentration that can be taken along with any major. You'll complete the program with the courses required for entry to PA school.

Clarkson University offers a Bachelor of Science degree with a major in biology and a concentration in pre-physician assistant studies. This program of study is designed specifically to meet the prerequisite courses for the Master of Science in Physician Assistant Studies program at Clarkson. In addition, our curriculum provides for most, if not all, of the course requirements for PA programs across the United States. You will have access to our pre-health advisor. ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
Description: Psychology is the scientific study of the mind, the brain and behavior. As a psychology major, you will examine the many factors that influence human and animal behavior, from the function of single brain cells to the effects of culture on the individual. You will also learn about the scientific methods used to conduct psychological research. The undergraduate psychology program at Clarkson is structured around the core disciplines in the field: cognitive, social, developmental, clinical and biological psychology. The major is designed to build a strong base of knowledge in all of these areas and give you hands-on experience by applying what you learn in the classroom to a lab setting. You'll complete several research projects and have the opportunity to participate in a variety of other high-impact learning experiences, including co-ops, internships, study abroad and community-based service learning. The psychology program is intentionally flexible to allow you to tailor your education to your career goals. Whether you plan on seeking a career right after graduation or continuing your education in graduate school, we will help you build a program of study that's right for you.

The BSSS program is an excellent opportunity for students who have an interest in combining their core science and liberal arts coursework into a personalized program of study. The curriculum requires that students select a focus in a science area (biology, chemistry, physics or mathematics). BSSS students also select a complementary non-science minor in areas such as business, communications or pre-health sciences advising tracks.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Social Sciences
Concentration: ['Criminology', 'Economics', 'History', 'Political Science', 'Psychology', 'Sociology', 'Quality of Life Studies']
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in Social Sciences (SS) is an interdisciplinary program that applies social science theories, concepts, and methods to the study of important societal issues. The Social Sciences major is the largest major in the Department of Humanities and Social Sciences. Its flexible degree requirements allow you to create an individualized course of study suited to your interests and career goals. Social science majors complete a minimum of one social science concentration. They are strongly encouraged to complete a second concentration, a minor, or a second major. Our students have paired the SS major with a second major in engineering, business, and the arts and sciences.

Through your classes, you will acquire core skills in research and writing, critical reading and analysis, and public speaking. In a world of increasing complexity and rapid change, these are the transferable skills that employers and graduate schools demand. The research and analytical skills that you develop as a Social Sciences major will prepare you for careers in law, public policy, nonprofit management, market research, urban planning and a wide range of other professions. Many of our majors go on to graduate school to earn an MA, MBA, JD, or PhD.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Social Documentation
Description:
The social documentation major at Clarkson is an interdisciplinary program that teaches students how to use documentary storytelling techniques to represent the lived experiences of others, paying particular attention to the complex intersections of culture, society and politics. Students in this program will study the ethical, social and political dimensions of documentary work while also developing a set of practical skills in media production. We offer a mix of theoretical, historical and production-based coursework designed to help students think critically about the role of media in society and also participate in the production of media content in an informed way.

Social documentation majors learn to research, write, produce, direct, shoot and edit non-fiction films, and they learn how to think critically about the stories we tell through media. Students study the historical, theoretical and ethical dimensions of documentary film, and they gain a strong foundation in the use of contemporary production technologies to tell compelling and powerful stories. The social documentation curriculum is hands-on and project-based. Students will build a portfolio of documentary work that reflects their unique interests and career goals. Students have the opportunity to participate in one of our many off-campus study programs, including a popular semester-long program in New York City.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sociology
Requirements:
To be considered for freshman admission, a student must submit the following:

3. A recommendation from a school counselor or a teacher.

Description: Sociology is the scientific study of human social behavior. Sociologists examine the ways in which people organize themselves into groups, from families to nations, and the resulting impact on individuals and their daily lives. Sociologists are interested in who we are, what we do, what we think and feel, and why. At Clarkson, sociology students examine the structure and culture of different societies and how those societies interact. They study issues such as rural and urban life, the intersection of science and society, race and ethnicity, deviance and crime, gender roles and inequalities, and how institutions like education, government, healthcare, and religion shape our lives. Sociology provides an excellent liberal arts education and develops strong critical thinking, research, and communication skills applicable to a wide variety of careers in social work, public administration, law, business, education, policy analysis, advocacy, and counseling.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Software Engineering

Software engineers design and develop software systems that are safe, secure and reliable. You will learn to use computer science, engineering and mathematics principles to design, develop and test software. At Clarkson, we have a project-based curriculum where you will gain hands-on experience building various software systems. As part of the program, you will work on team-based projects and learn skills in project management, ethical and professional responsibilities, and effective communication.

Our students have had co-ops or internships with companies like Amazon, Google, IBM, Microsoft, Netflix, Pfizer, Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics and Capital One.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Statistics
Description: Statistics is the science and art of learning from data. Statisticians offer essential insight into nearly every field imaginable, including business, science, technology, government and engineering. As a statistician, you'll apply mathematical and statistical knowledge to scientific, industrial and economic problems. Our statistics program will prepare you to enter the workforce with real-world skills and knowledge you can immediately put to use. Or you can continue your education with graduate study in statistics, actuarial science, business, economics or another related field. What you learn as a statistics major will also make you a more discerning consumer of information and a better-informed citizen. Our program will train you in the theory and practice of statistics. We will prepare you to make valid inferences from data in the real world. You'll learn to model uncertainty and to distinguish between random and significant effects. You will explore experimental design, regression analysis, machine learning, artificial intelligence, statistical theory, time series analysis, categorical data analysis and mathematical statistics. Throughout our program, you'll learn to be a strong communicator, both orally and in writing. You will be able to explain the assumptions of a model, justify a particular statistical analysis and describe its limitations.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is https://www.clarkson.edu.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sustainable Energy Systems Engineering
Department: Wallace H. Coulter School of Engineering
Description: The world has a challenge ahead of it to meet an increasing global energy demand while mitigating the global environmental impact. It is clear that we need a workforce trained to design, build, operate and maintain sustainable and resilient energy systems. The Bachelor of Science in Sustainable Energy Systems Engineering (SESE) program is a specialized undergraduate engineering program that provides a fundamental basis in engineering and a multidisciplinary systems perspective to address society’s need for clean, affordable, and sustainable energy. The curriculum focuses on energy systems analysis and design, from components to large-scale systems. You will gain in-depth knowledge and skills in the following three primary focus areas: Energy generation and conversion, such as solar, wind, biomass and geothermal. Energy transmission, storage and distribution. Energy efficiency and demand management.

Description: As a sustainable environmental systems major, you will learn to solve environmental challenges using a systems-thinking approach. This unique major is a partnership between the Institute for a Sustainable Environment and the Coulter School of Engineering. It prepares you to tackle complex environmental issues from a holistic perspective. You will become a problem solver who can apply engineering and scientific principles to address environmental challenges. Our major helps you to develop the technical skills to collect and analyze environmental data. You will also learn to work in interdisciplinary teams to find sustainable solutions that consider the environmental, social and economic impacts of those decisions. This program prepares you for graduate school or a career in the government, private or nonprofit sectors.

This program is a great option for students who are looking for a program that is not available at Clarkson but can be created by combining several areas of study. It is also an ideal choice for transfer students who may have credits from other institutions that they wish to combine into a single degree.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in War and Peace Studies
Requirements: To apply as a first-year student, you will need the Common Application or Clarkson Application, an official high school transcript, and one letter of recommendation from a school counselor or teacher. Standardized test scores are optional.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in War and Peace Studies at Clarkson University is a new, innovative major that examines one of the most fundamental problems of human existence: the organized use of violence. Why do humans go to war? Are there certain conditions that make war more or less likely? How has warfare changed over time and how is it likely to change in the future? What are the human, economic, and political costs of war? What can we learn from past wars? What are the essential components of a just and lasting peace? This interdisciplinary major will train you to become a critical thinker about issues related to war, peace, security, and global affairs. Our core curriculum combines history, social science, and humanities. You'll take courses on military history, the sociology of war and peace, the politics of security, and the ethics of war. This strong foundation will position you to succeed in both our upper-level courses and your chosen career field. You can tailor your education to fit your interests and career goals with our diverse electives and a large number of free electives that will allow you to explore minors or even a second major in one of our many complementary programs, like political science or history. With a degree in war and peace studies from Clarkson, you'll be well-prepared for careers in foreign service, intelligence analysis, homeland security, humanitarian aid, journalism, international law and business, and more.

ANTH311 Gender and Globalization

Anthropologists are interested in how societies are organized and why people from different cultures behave in the ways they do. The minor in anthropology at Clarkson complements any area of study. The minor provides an added dimension to the student's primary academic focus by helping them understand different cultures and societies. This is especially useful for students interested in studying abroad and/or working for an international company.

Description: The architectural and facilities engineering minor is a cross-disciplinary minor that introduces engineering and non-engineering students to the challenges of designing, constructing and operating buildings and other facilities. ProgramName: Minor in Biology
Description: Biology is the study of life, and in this minor you'll explore that topic from the molecular to the ecosystem level. Students minoring in biology at Clarkson benefit from our small class sizes, one-on-one attention from faculty and access to state-of-the-art facilities and equipment. Whether you want to perform independent research with a faculty member, study pre-health or develop another biology-related professional interest, you'll be on your way to success with a minor in biology. Our minor is flexible. Our core curriculum gives you a strong foundation in all areas of biology. Then, you can customize the program by choosing electives from a wide range of subjects, including animal behavior, cancer biology, immunology, microbiology, and molecular cell biology.

Description: Biomolecular science is an interdisciplinary field that lies at the interface of biology, chemistry and physics. Students pursuing a minor in biomolecular science at Clarkson can expect to explore topics in biochemistry, biophysics, cell biology and molecular biology, among others. These courses will help you gain valuable insight and prepare you for a professional career in the medical field or in graduate studies.
